clue.text: Someone includes the county cricketer

indicators.note: the word for someone holds the county inside it, as a box includes its contents

parts.note: a man is someone, any person
Clare is a county in the west of Ireland

explanation.surface: A person is said to number a county cricket player among their acquaintances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts CLARE inside MAN. Archie MacLaren was an England cricket captain of the early 1900s, who played county cricket for Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: Archie MacLaren was a famous Lancashire and England batsman and captain.

clue.text: Joint holder ?

parts.note: a joint here is a joint of meat, not a body joint or a shared owner, and its holder is the cupboard it is kept in

explanation.definitionFit: A larder cupboard with a mesh front keeps a roast or other cut of meat safe from flies.

clue.text: Lowers his charges ?

parts.note: read 'lowers' as 'things that moo' (to low is to moo), not 'reduces'; his charges are the animals he looks after

explanation.definitionFit: A herdsman tends cows, which low, so the animals in his charge are lowing beasts.

clue.text: Concede a penny rise to little Cratchit

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for a penny in old British money

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the name upwards, so it is written backwards

parts.note: Tiny Tim is the youngest Cratchit in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

explanation.surface: A small pay rise of a penny is grudgingly granted to young Tim Cratchit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns TIM upwards to give MIT, after A and D. The surface recalls Scrooge, who gives Bob Cratchit's family very little.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to concede that it is true.

clue.text: "Half in love with —— Death" (Keats)

parts.note: a line from Keats's Ode to a Nightingale with one word left out, before Death: fill the gap

explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a dash where the missing word goes: the full line is 'I have been half in love with easeful Death'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats calls death restful and full of comfort in Ode to a Nightingale, the word that fills the quoted line.

clue.text: She went to court to save a pound

definitions.text: She went to court to save a pound

parts.words: She went to court to save a pound
parts.note: the pound is Shylock's pound of flesh, which Antonio owes in The Merchant of Venice; the woman disguised as a lawyer wins the case

explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice the heroine argues in court so that Antonio need not give up a pound of flesh.

clue.text: Protest is something no-one backs

parts.note: an object is a thing, something

indicators.note: in this clue the word 'backs' means the phrase no-one is written in reverse order

parts.note: no plus one, with I as the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A complaint is called one that nobody supports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns NO + I (one) round to give ION after OBJECT. 'backs' looks like 'supports', but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An objection is a protest raised against something.

clue.text: Does office work of sorts

definitions.meaning: taps out letters on a keyboard, as a secretary does

explanation.surface: Someone does clerical jobs of various kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: A typist keys documents, and kinds or categories are also called this.

clue.text: Temper of girl and boy

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
Al is a boy's name, short for Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: Two children, a girl and a boy, are described by their mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' reads as mood but here is the metalworker's verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To anneal glass or metal is to toughen it by heating and slow cooling, which is to temper it.

clue.text: Contrive to find race time

parts.note: man means the human race, mankind
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone schemes to discover what time a race starts.
explanation.definitionFit: To contrive is to manage to do something, bringing it about by effort.

clue.text: Times bursting into song in the plant

indicators.note: the word into says the shuffled letters go inside the word for a song

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

indicators.note: bursting breaks the word Times apart so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper is suddenly singing about a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursting' rearranges TIMES to TEMIS, which 'into' puts inside ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a genus of aromatic herbs including wormwood and mugwort.

clue.text: Butterfly country

parts.note: Butterfly is Madame Butterfly, Puccini's opera, and the country is where she lives

explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's Madama Butterfly is set in Nagasaki, so her homeland is the Far Eastern island nation.

clue.text: Rent place in Yugo-Slavia ?

definitions.meaning: a rent is a tear or division, a noun
a port on the Dalmatian coast, then in Yugoslavia, now in Croatia; the hyphen divides the country's name

explanation.surface: Someone asks about letting a house in Yugoslavia.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'Yugo-Slavia' shows the name broken into two, a hint at the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear or crack is a division, and the Adriatic port is a city once in Yugoslavia, now in Croatia.

clue.text: Italian girl needs money-—odd case

parts.note: a franc is a unit of money, used in France and Switzerland

indicators.note: something odd is out of order, so the word case is rearranged

explanation.surface: An Italian girl is short of money, which makes her case a strange one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges CASE to ESCA after FRANC.
explanation.definitionFit: Francesca is an Italian girl's name, as in Dante's Francesca da Rimini.

clue.text: This artery spells the undoing of Mr. Lea

indicators.note: undoing the words of Mr Lea takes them apart so their letters can be rebuilt

explanation.surface: A blocked blood vessel proves the downfall of a man named Lea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the undoing' rearranges the seven letters OFMRLEA. 'spells' looks like 'means' but just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The femoral artery is the main blood vessel of the thigh.

clue.text: Artist uses odd term about Ibsen's. work

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go around the name of the play
odd says the letters of the word term are in a strange order

parts.note: Brand is an 1865 verse play by Henrik Ibsen

explanation.surface: A painter makes strange use of a term about a work by Ibsen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges TERM to REMT, and 'about' puts it around BRAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt van Rijn was the great Dutch painter of the 17th century.

clue.text: Priest has replaced prophet

parts.note: Eli is the priest at Shiloh in the Old Testament, who raised Samuel

indicators.note: replaced means the word has is put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A priest has been swapped for a prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges HAS to SHA after ELI.
explanation.definitionFit: Elisha was an Old Testament prophet, successor to Elijah.

clue.text: Female has another upset, indisposed in London

parts.note: her is the female pronoun

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word for a hen upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: another female, a hen being a female bird
ill means unwell, indisposed

explanation.surface: A woman has another woman who is upset and unwell in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another female, a HEN, which 'upset' turns up to NEH. HERNE HILL is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: This south London district lies near Brixton and Dulwich, so it is a place found in the capital.

clue.text: Bob drinks and does a spot or so of painting

definitions.text: does a spot or so of painting

parts.note: a bob is a shilling, abbreviated s in old British money
to tipple is to drink alcohol

explanation.surface: A man called Bob drinks and dabbles in painting.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the old British shilling, written s. 'Bob' looks like a name, but it gives the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipple is to paint with small dots or dabs rather than strokes.

clue.text: No gems ordered from Zurich ?

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of no gems are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A jeweller's order from Switzerland arrives without any stones.
explanation.walkthrough: The gnomes of Zurich were Swiss bankers, a phrase from 1960s British politics; ordering gems from Zurich fits their trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiss bankers were called the gnomes of Zurich by British politicians, so the bankers are those from that city.

clue.text: Runs in music ?

definitions.meaning: runs and goals totted up are points made in a game
the written parts of a piece of music are kept in these sheets

explanation.surface: Runs in a piece of music, the quick scales a player rattles off.
explanation.definitionFit: Points totals and written music share one word: tallies of a game, and the printed parts of a composition.

clue.text: Are dividing a lot of money in the tower

indicators.note: dividing means the word are splits the money word in two by sitting inside it

parts.note: a mint is a large sum of money, as in 'made a mint'

explanation.surface: A fortune is shared out in a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dividing' puts ARE inside MINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque.

clue.text: U.S. president brings up mother — and one child

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing up the word for a mother reads it upwards, so in reverse

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, such as a horse
I is the Roman numeral for one
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A president raises his mother and one child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings up' turns DAM upwards to MAD. 'brings up' looks like raising children, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison was the fourth president of the United States.

clue.text: Request change of air for an African soldier

parts.note: to request is to ask

indicators.note: a change of the word air means its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A soldier in Africa asks for a change of scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' rearranges AIR to ARI after ASK.
explanation.definitionFit: An askari was a local soldier serving the European colonial powers in East Africa.

clue.text: Weapon to wear inside, but not in the drawing-room

indicators.note: inside means the word wear goes within the word for a weapon

parts.note: a sword is a weapon

explanation.surface: A gentleman should wear his sword indoors, but not in the drawing-room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts WEAR inside SWORD. A drawing-room is a polite sitting room, where such language is out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath or obscenity is a word unsuited to polite company, such as a drawing-room.

clue.text: Cape, point and mount in Germany

indicators.note: in a down clue to mount is to climb, so the cape and point are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a ness is a cape or headland, as in Loch Ness
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A list of landmarks: a cape, a point and a mountain in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' turns NESS + E upwards. 'mount' looks like a mountain in the list, but it is the reversal signal. ESSEN is a city in the Ruhr.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr, in western Germany.

clue.text: Bob, the Dickensian animal

parts.note: a bob is a shilling, abbreviated s in old British money
Uriah Heep is the creeping clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: Bob is described as an animal from a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the old British shilling, written s. 'Bob' looks like a name again, and Bob Cratchit is Dickensian, but it gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: A flock animal kept for wool and meat is an animal.

clue.text: Is back with fresh strength

indicators.note: back means the word is is written backwards

parts.note: fresh means new

explanation.surface: Someone returns with renewed vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IS to SI before NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew means muscular strength, as in 'the sinews of war'.

clue.text: An heir for the old admiral

parts.note: a son is an heir

explanation.surface: An heir is chosen to succeed an old admiral.
explanation.definitionFit: George Anson was an 18th-century British admiral who sailed round the world.

clue.text: Necessary to have 24 lit ? A possibility

parts.note: the answer to clue 24, the German city

indicators.note: a possibility is one arrangement the letters of lit and a could take

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the city must be lit up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibility' rearranges LIT A to TIAL after ESSEN, the answer to 24 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential is necessary, indispensable.

clue.text: I get in materials for fire

indicators.note: materials for says the letters of i get in are the raw stuff from which the answer is built

explanation.surface: Someone gathers in wood and kindling to make a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'materials for' rearranges the letters of I GET IN. 'fire' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire something is to set it alight, kindle it.

clue.text: Where desk-workers went" for their dips

definitions.text: Where desk-workers went" for their dips

parts.words: Where desk-workers went" for their dips
parts.note: the desk-workers are schoolchildren and their dips are dips of the pen, not swims in a pool

explanation.definitionFit: Old school desks had small pots of ink sunk into them, where pupils dipped their pens.
